uutiset.t: Nigeria Boosts Retail Supply of Dollars to Curb Naira Volatility
uutiset.s: The Central Bank of Nigeria approved a large increase in the sale of dollars to retail customers as it sought to boost local liquidity and ease pressure on the naira, which has lost ground this month.

uutiset.t: ECB Officials Saw More Tightening With Inflation Outlook Worse
uutiset.s: European Central Bank officials meeting last month envisaged tightening monetary policy further in the future after the outlook for inflation worsened.

uutiset.t: Altria, Japan Tobacco Explore Breakup of Imperial Brands
uutiset.s: Altria Group Inc. and Japan Tobacco Inc. are exploring a potential breakup of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands Plc, in what would be one of the largest takeovers of a UK company in a decade.

uutiset.t: UBS Vows to Remain Global as Swiss Capital Outlook Darkens
uutiset.s: UBS Group AG’s top leadership wrote to employees this week in an attempt to reassure them that Switzerland’s ongoing efforts to tighten regulation won’t take away something that the bank has worked for decades to build — a truly global business.

uutiset.t: Global Stocks Climb as AI Trade Rebounds
uutiset.s: Stocks rose as investors in Europe and Asia tracked a comeback in technology shares on Wall Street, with days of sharp swings likely to give way to thin holiday trading. Europe’s Stoxx 600 jumped as much as 1.7%, with gains following late-session dip buying in the US that pulled the Nasdaq 100 back

uutiset.t: Kim Shannon of Sionna Tops Market With Bet on Cheap Value Picks
uutiset.s: A veteran fund manager is beating benchmark indices by betting on undervalued Canadian stocks.

uutiset.t: Brazil Tightens Consumer Lending Rules as Household Debt Soars
uutiset.s: Brazil’s central bank unveiled measures to curb excessive consumer borrowing as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva grows concerned about soaring household debt.

uutiset.t: Congo Pitches $15 Billion Infrastructure Deals as Mining Booms
uutiset.s: Democratic Republic of Congo is pitching $15 billion in rail and other infrastructure projects as it rides a copper mining boom that the government hopes will transform trade and transport in the central African nation.

uutiset.t: BBVA Weighs SRT to Hedge About $500 Million of Data Center Loans
uutiset.s: BBVA SA is considering a deal that would offload risk on about €500 million ($547 million) of data center loans, as banks worldwide explore multiple ways to hedge their exposure to artificial intelligence-related infrastructure.

uutiset.t: Congo Closes on Top Copper Supplier Chile as Exports Soar Again
uutiset.s: The Democratic Republic of Congo is closing the gap on the world’s top copper producer Chile, after quarterly exports topped 1 million tons for the first time in the three months through September.

uutiset.t: Inflation-Wary Shoppers Prepare for Black Friday
uutiset.s: Retailers had plenty of reasons to be worried about this year’s holiday season, but the latest round of earnings, from Dick’s Sporting Goods Inc. to Kohl’s Corp. and Dollar Tree Inc., show that shoppers are still spending briskly, despite their concerns about rising costs. Bloomberg's Shaquille Omar

uutiset.t: China’s Copper Crunch Hides a Fragile Demand Outlook
uutiset.s: A near-term supply squeeze is more easily fixed than weaker economic growth.

uutiset.t: Trump’s China Tariffs Threaten Fresh Trade Tensions
uutiset.s: China has vowed to defend its interests after the US unveiled new tariffs on Chinese goods and warned the rate could double if trade talks collapse, injecting fresh tension ahead of a planned meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. uutiset.t: Turkey Plans Lower Taxes on Lira Deposits to Support Currency
uutiset.s: Turkey is planning to lower taxes on interest from lira deposits to support demand for the currency following a sharp decline in official foreign-exchange reserves, according to people familiar with the matter.

uutiset.t: Turkey’s Traders See Slower Rate Cut Pace as Reserves Shrink
uutiset.s: Traders are dialing back bets on a December interest-rate cut in Turkey following a sharp drop in central bank reserves, raising concerns that policymakers may have a harder time supporting the lira.
